pages.text: Sound in a fluid flowing faster than sound cannot make headway upstream. Where the flow crosses its own speed of sound there is a horizon for sound - and the mathematics of sound near it is the mathematics of light near a black hole. Hawking radiation included.

The $(item)Analog Black Hole$() makes the flow out of $(fluid)Bose-Einstein Condensate$(): it streams toward a laser step, subsonic, and falls over it, thinned and fast - supersonic. Set the density (sound speed grows as its square root), the flow and the step depth so that both hold.

At the horizon phonon pairs appear, one carried off downstream, its partner escaping up: a glow at $(thing)T_H = ħκ/2πk_B$(), a few nanokelvin. The condensate itself must be colder than that to see it, and the correlations summed over many shots. Nothing but Bose-Einstein Condensate is cold enough as the coolant.
